annotation.speech2: Five concentric circles centred at the origin in the x y plane, each drawn in a different colour and labelled with a value of c. The smallest, in amber, is c equals three quarters; going outwards they are c equals one half, c equals zero, c equals negative one, and the largest, in black, is c equals negative two.
The level curve where f equals three quarters, a circle of radius one half. It is the innermost circle, so the largest values of f occur near the origin.
The level curve where f equals one half, a circle of radius one over root two.
The level curve where f equals zero, the unit circle.
The level curve where f equals negative one, a circle of radius root two.
The level curve where f equals negative two, a circle of radius root three. The circles spread further apart as c decreases, which tells us the surface is steepest near the rim.
